dossier.public_summary: The signal is a flat-bottomed 2.5-hour dip seen in two sectors on a nearby K-dwarf where no nearby star within a TESS pixel can mimic it and no odd-even or secondary eclipse is seen. The depth implies a 3.2 Earth-radius planet, with a duration that matches the star's size, so a planet is the best explanation despite a low classifier score. Depth differs between the two sectors (1106 vs 2259 ppm) and the dip is below SNR 7, so further confirmation is needed.

reasons.why: strongly flat-bottomed transit shape favours planet over V-shaped stellar eclipse
undiluted radius 3.242 Rearth is planet-sized, well below stellar regime, positively favouring planet
no star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly produce the dip; closest that could is 54.1 arcsec needing 0.0384 dip, so neighbour eclipse is ruled out
observed 2.5 h duration is close to central 3.593 h for 0.707 Rsun star; stellar_radius tool gives ratio 0.7/0.75 with FLAME radius, planet size 3.24/3.07 Rearth consistent
odd-even difference 0.4192 (1417 vs 2439 ppm) below 4σ threshold, not significant binary signature
no significant secondary (snr 3.818 <5 and below best_brightening_snr 3.923); hot giant secondary would be similar
low rank but outweighed by on-target flat dip with planet size and no blend; similar signals include both planets and binaries, verdict based on checks not rank
